newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium spread narrows on LME, January tightens.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium spread narrows on LME, January tightens.

text.p: The contango for cash/threes aluminium on the London Metal Exchange (LME) narrowed in on Wednesday, reflecting persistent borrowing of the January 1997 date, traders said.

Cash/threes was at a contango of $20/21, against $26 on Tuesday, and compared with "full financing" levels nearer $30. There was a premium of $6 paid to borrow metal from the January date for one day. Jan/threes showed a $5 backwardation, against level on Tuesday.
Traders said the market is heavily short in January 1997, largely from the speculative side, with metal for the relevant dates held in strong hands.
Some said the borrowing was precautionary, ahead of a repeat of similar tightness seen in January 1996 when sizeable backwardations flared up.
"There may be nearly a million tonnes of metal on warrant, but that does not necessarily mean it is all available," one said.
LME warehouse inventories currently stand at 966,000 tonnes. However, the bulk of this metal - 313,725 tonnes - is held in Liverpool which is an expensive warehouse to lift material from, some said.

The tightness in January which has developed this week has helped three months prices move up, although the advances have not been substantial. Analysts see the market remaining rangebound, basis a floor at $1,400, and $1,440/50 - an area where producers will be looking to sell.
Prices were quoted at $1,433/34 a tonne, some $10 above levels seen earlier in the week.
